name: Germany — German parties
intro: compare it with German political parties
inclusion_note: The test includes the main national parties of Germany: those represented in the Bundestag and those with a significant national following. Positions are the team's estimates and are open to review.
hemicycle_note: Seats in the Bundestag after the February 2025 federal election, arranged left to right. Approximate. 630 members.

Linke.name: Die Linke
Linke.priorities: Affordable housing, Cost of living, Taxing wealth, Public services, Diplomacy with Russia, no arms deliveries
Linke.description: Democratic-socialist party that made a strong comeback in 2025, driven by young voters. It focuses on rents, prices and taxing the rich, and opposes arms exports.

BSW.name: Bündnis Sahra Wagenknecht
BSW.ideologies: Left conservatism, Left-wing populism, Sovereignism, Euroscepticism
BSW.priorities: Diplomacy with Russia, no arms deliveries, Cost of living, Reducing immigration, Workers' rights and wages, Protecting national industry
BSW.description: Split from Die Linke led by Sahra Wagenknecht. It combines left-wing economics with restrictive migration policy, opposes arms deliveries to Ukraine and wants cheaper energy through dialogue with Russia. It narrowly missed the Bundestag in 2025.

SPD.name: Sozialdemokratische Partei Deutschlands
SPD.priorities: Workers' rights and wages, Public services, Affordable housing, Defence and support for Ukraine, Protecting national industry
SPD.description: Germany's oldest party, now junior partner in Friedrich Merz's coalition after a historic low in 2025. It defends pensions, the minimum wage and industrial jobs.

Grüne.name: Bündnis 90/Die Grünen
Grüne.ideologies: Green politics, Social liberalism, Pro-Europeanism, Atlanticism
Grüne.priorities: Climate action, Defence and support for Ukraine, Deeper European integration, Civil liberties, Digital innovation
Grüne.description: Germany's green party, in the federal government from 2021 to 2025. Strongly pro-European and firm on support for Ukraine, it opposes nuclear power and backs a fast energy transition.

FDP.name: Freie Demokratische Partei
FDP.priorities: Fiscal discipline, Lower taxes, Less red tape, Digital innovation, Education
FDP.description: Germany's classical-liberal party, defender of the debt brake and lower taxes. Its exit from the governing coalition in 2024 triggered early elections, after which it fell out of the Bundestag.

CDU/CSU.name: CDU/CSU (Union)
CDU/CSU.ideologies: Christian democracy, Liberal conservatism, Pro-Europeanism, Atlanticism
CDU/CSU.priorities: Competitiveness and growth, Reducing immigration, Defence and support for Ukraine, Security and law and order, Less red tape
CDU/CSU.description: The Christian-democratic alliance of the CDU and its Bavarian sister the CSU, which won the 2025 election and leads the government under Chancellor Friedrich Merz. It favours tighter migration rules, economic revival and higher defence spending.

AfD.name: Alternative für Deutschland
AfD.priorities: Remigration and closed borders, National sovereignty, Diplomacy with Russia, no arms deliveries, Cost of living, Nuclear energy
AfD.description: Far-right party that came second in 2025 with its best result ever. It calls for 'remigration', leaving the euro and possibly the EU, an end to sanctions on Russia and a return to nuclear and fossil energy. Parts of it are monitored by German intelligence as extremist.
